πνευματικὰ συγκρίνοντες, τῷ συνεξετάζειν τήνδε τὴν λέξιν τῇδε τῇ λέξει καὶ τὰ
ὅμοια συνάγειν, ἀνακαλύπτεται ὡσπερεὶ ὁ νοῦς τῆς γραφῆς. οὕτω γὰρ συνίημι τὰ
τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ γίνομαι διδακτὸς πνεύματος· οὐ μόνον <τῷ> τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος
μεμαθηκέναι τοῦ κινήσαντος τὸν Ἡσαΐαν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα ἐσχηκέναι
ὅπερ ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν τοὺς Ἡσαΐου λόγους· εἰ μὴ γὰρ τὸ πνεῦμα ἀνοίξῃ τοὺς
λόγους τῶν προφητῶν, οὐ δύναται ἀνοixθῆναι τὰ κεκλεισμένα. Ἐπεὶ δὲ ταῦτα εἶπεν,
ἀναγκαίως ἐπιφέρει ὅτι εἰσί τινες ἄνθρωποι μὴ παρα δεχόμενοι τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος
τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐ διὰ τὴν φύσιν ὡς οἴονται οἱ ἑτερό δοξοι ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ μὴ παρεσκευακέναι
ἑαυτούς. ψυχικὸς γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος, ψυχικὸς γὰρ ἦν· ὅτε
<δὲ> ἔκλινεν εἰς θεοσέβειαν καὶ παρεδέξατο τὸ πνεῦμα, γέγονε πνευματικός. καὶ οὐ
δύναται γνῶναι ὁ ψυχικὸς ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται· οὐκ οἶδεν διὰ τοῦτο <ὃ>
ἀκούει ὅτι ἀνακρίνεται πνευματικῶς, καὶ δοκιμαζομένη γε ἡ δύναμι ἐλέγχει τοὺ
ἄφρονα οἷον ἐὰν λέγω ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος διδαχθείς, καὶ δυνάμει λέγω, καὶ ὁ
ἀκροατὴς δοκιμάζων τὴν δύναμιν δοκῇ καὶ μὴ συγκατάθηται, δοκιμαζομένη ἡ
δύναμι ἐλέγχει τοὺ ἄφρονα . καὶ ἔστιν οὐχ ὡς ἐκεῖνος ἀποδο κιμάσας τὸ λεγόμενον
ὅσον τὸ λεγόμενον ἀπεδοκίμασεν ἐκεῖνον· εἰ γὰρ κακότεχνον ψυχὴν οὐκ
εἰ ελεύ εται οφία οὐδὲ κατοική ει ἐν ώματι κατάχρεῳ ἁμαρτία . Ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς
ἀνακρίνει μὲν πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ' οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται. ὁ μηκέτι κατὰ άρκα
περιπατῶν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα καὶ ἀεὶ τῇ ἐπιμελείᾳ αὔξων αὐτὸ καὶ ἀναζωπυρῶν τὸ
χάρι μα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ πλεῖον, ἑαυτῷ κατασκευάζει τὸ γενέσθαι πνευματικός·

pass_a_gloss: Continues: taught from the Spirit—understood from apostolic words. Comparing spiritual with spiritual: examine wording with wording, gather likes; Scripture’s mind is uncovered. Thus understand God’s things and become taught by the Spirit—not only learning what moved Isaiah but having the Spirit that sealed Isaiah’s words; without Spirit opening, sealed prophetic words stay shut. He adds: some do not receive things of the Spirit—not by nature as heterodox claim but from lack of preparation. Soulish does not receive things of the Spirit; when turned to piety and receiving Spirit, becomes spiritual. Soulish cannot know he is spiritually examined; tested power convicts the fool—taught by the Spirit powerful speech rejected by hearer means the speech rejects him; wisdom enters no plotting evil soul nor body owed to sin. Spiritual examines all, examined by none. Walking by Spirit, growing and kindling God’s gift, one becomes spiritual and can examine Greeks, barbarians, wise, fools; none can examine him for greatness of mind and reasonings. Know spiritual by fruits: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self control—where these, Spirit and spiritual; missing any, not yet. Lemma 1 Cor 3:1–3a: could not speak as to spiritual but fleshly, infants in Christ; milk not solid food—unable then and still. Origen: hearers include perfect spiritual (as above) and not spiritual believers—infants and fleshly in Christ (‘in Christ’ common). Imperfect, unexercised in Scripture need lesser lessons called milk. Spiritual foods scale: milk, food, true food, solid food, Word’s flesh, spiritual vegetable—backed by Scripture; not every spiritual food is ‘true food’ (my flesh is true food). Not solid: weaker ethical teaching by concession for weak hearers. Solid ethical: perfect chastity, virginity/temperance, martyrdom. Mystical solid: Father and Son. Law sometimes solid, sometimes lesser. Snakes killing murmurers: simple ‘do not murmur’; mystical—who snakes are, snake on wood, salvation by looking—so each spiritual text. Who get milk: Peter shows in the—cut. Also: comparing wording with wording uncovers the mind of Scripture; become taught by the Spirit by having the Spirit that sealed Isaiah; sealed prophetic words open only by the Spirit. Refusal of Spirit things is not by nature but lack of preparation; soulish becomes spiritual when receiving the Spirit. Tested power convicts the fool; wisdom will not enter a soul plotting evil. Spiritual examines all peoples and teachings and is examined by none; known by fruit of the Spirit: love joy peace patience kindness goodness faith gentleness self control. Infants in Christ get milk not solid food; scale of spiritual foods from milk to flesh of the Word; weaker ethical teaching is concession; solid ethical teaching includes chastity virginity martyrdom; mystical solid food is Father and Son. Law sometimes solid sometimes lesser; snakes of murmuring read simply or mystically with the snake on the wood.
pass_b_english: Spirit is to be understood from the apostolic words: “comparing spiritual things with spiritual”—by examining this wording with that wording and gathering like with like, the mind of Scripture is uncovered as it were. In this way I understand the things of God and become taught by the Spirit: not only by having learned the things of the Spirit that moved Isaiah, but also by having the same Spirit that shut and sealed Isaiah’s words; for unless the Spirit opens the prophets’ words, what is shut cannot be opened. And since he said these things, he necessarily adds that there are some people who do not receive the things of the Spirit of God—not because of nature, as the heterodox suppose, but because they have not prepared themselves. For the soulish person does not receive the things of the Spirit—he was soulish; but when he inclined toward piety and received the Spirit, he became spiritual. And the soulish cannot know that he is examined spiritually; therefore he does not know, about what he hears, that it is examined spiritually; and when the power is tested it convicts the fool—as when I speak taught by the Spirit and speak with power, and the hearer testing the power thinks otherwise and does not assent: the power being tested convicts the fool. And it is not so much that he has rejected what is said as that what is said has rejected him; for “wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil, nor dwell in a body in debt to sin.” “The spiritual person examines all things, yet he himself is examined by no one.” The one who no longer walks according to flesh but according to Spirit, and always by care grows it and kindles more the gift of God, prepares for himself to become spiritual; and having become so he is able to examine all things—the Greeks’, the barbarians’, the wise’, the senseless’; and no one can examine him because of the greatness of his understanding and of his reasonings. And if you want to recognize the spiritual person, “by their fruits you will know them.” What then are the fruits of the Spirit by which one must know who is spiritual? Hear the apostle: “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self control”; where these are, there is the Spirit, and that one is spiritual; and where any of these is missing, that one is not yet spiritual.

On 1 Corinthians 3:1–3a: “And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people but as to fleshly, as to infants in Christ. I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able; but neither are you able even now.” Origen: of hearers some are perfect—the spiritual, of whom we were also speaking earlier; and those who are not spiritual yet believe in Christ are, as the apostle says, infants in Christ and fleshly in Christ—for I hear “in Christ” as common to both. So those not yet more perfect and not yet exercised in the sacred Scriptures need lesser lessons, which the apostle named milk: “I gave you milk to drink, not solid food; for you were not yet able, but neither are you able even now.” And I think there is a scale among spiritual foods: milk, food, true food, solid food, flesh of the Word, and spiritual vegetable. And I dare to say this persuaded by the Scriptures; for he did not say every spiritual food is true food when he says, “My flesh is true food.” What then is not solid food? The more ethical teachings and whatever among ethical matters is weaker—said by way of concession, not by command, stewarded because of the hearers’ weakness. But whatever more perfect teaching among ethical matters belongs to eager and hardworking hearers—these I would call solid food among ethical teachings: teaching about perfect chastity, about virginity or temperance, about martyrdom; these are solid food. And solid food in mystical matters is teaching about Father and Son. So also the law sometimes hands on solid food, sometimes lesser. For example we come to the word about the snakes that killed the sons of Israel because of murmuring: if we read more simply, we say, “Let us not murmur, as some of them murmured and were destroyed by the snakes.” But if the hearer can hear a mystical word, we say who the snakes are and who the snake hung upon the wood, and how one is saved by looking to that snake—and so with each spiritual Scripture.
